description: Root Renovate preset for SLICC's web repos. Extend it with github>ai-ecoverse/slicc-shared-web and keep repo-specific rules in the repo's own renovate.json.
Every dependency updates in its own PR so a breaking bump fails in isolation; only purposeful cohesion groups exist, never a catch-all group.
Automerge is on: a PR merges by itself once CI is green and the release is old enough.

Go modules: run go mod tidy after every update, so a bump that changes indirect requirements or leaves the old version's go.sum lines passes go mod tidy -diff in CI, and rewrite import paths on major updates. This is set for every update, not in a gomod packageRule, because Renovate runs a branch's go.mod artifacts with the postUpdateOptions of the branch's first upgrade by dependency name, which in a group that also moves the npm package, such as @ai-ecoverse/slicc-browsers with github.com/ai-ecoverse/slicc-browsers, is the npm one.

customManagers.description: npm packages pinned by exact version in jsDelivr URLs inside sources, such as the tar library slicc-bios imports at runtime.

Versions pinned in workflow and action files, each annotated on the line above with # renovate: datasource=<datasource> depName=<name>, optionally followed by packageName=, versioning=, extractVersion= and registryUrl=. The version is the first one on the next line that follows a colon, an equals sign or an @, so it covers env: values, with: inputs, uses: refs and inline pkg@version installs.
matchStrings: # renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>[a-z-.]+?) depName=(?<depName>[^\s]+?)(?: packageName=(?<packageName>[^\s]+?))?(?: versioning=(?<versioning>[^\s]+?))?(?: extractVersion=(?<extractVersion>[^\s]+?))?(?: registryUrl=(?<registryUrl>[^\s]+?))?[ \t]*\r?\n[^\n]*?(?:[:=][ \t]*["']?|@)(?<currentValue>v?\d[^\s"'@,]*)

packageRules.description: Pin npm dependencies to exact versions so every change is a visible package.json diff in its own PR. engines and peerDependencies keep their ranges.
Major bumps wait longer: more risk of breaking changes and a more attractive target for malicious releases.

Our own packages and shared config ship together: take them as soon as they are released, ahead of the hourly PR limit, whether Renovate sees them by package name (npm, reusable workflows, git URLs, Go modules) or by dependency name.

Our own packages version their builds as <upstream version>-<build>, such as wasm-coreutils 9.12.0-6 or wasm-tls-engine 3.6.7-1, which Renovate reads as prereleases and by default never offers, so a pin like 3.6.5-1 never moves. Allow unstable versions, but never past the npm latest dist-tag, which homescoop moves only to certified builds, so a build that is only on stage or next is not offered.

Never offer a major of slicc-shared-web itself, as the npm package or as the ai-ecoverse/slicc-shared-web reusable workflow ref: the 2.x line drops node-ci.yml and changes the shared tooling, so a repo moves to the next major by hand. Minors and patches within the repo's current major still update and automerge.

slicc-shared-web moves as one: the npm package (harness/shard.cjs and the shared tooling) and the pipeline.yml workflow ref belong to the same release, and the pipeline needs the harness at its version or later, so both update in one PR. Both wait an hour after release: Renovate can serve a cached GitHub tag list for several minutes after the tag is pushed while npm already shows the new version, so a group offered at once can move the npm pin without the workflow ref.
fnox-build publishes @ai-ecoverse/fnox and its platform packages only as <upstream fnox version>-slicc.<build> prereleases, with latest pointing at the newest; take only the -slicc.N ones.
@ai-ecoverse/slicc-kernel and @ai-ecoverse/wasi-pnpm are certified together: move them in one PR, majors included, so they pass CI as a pair. A repo that pins only one of them still gets its PR.
@ai-ecoverse/wasm-coreutils and @ai-ecoverse/wasm-procps are certified together: move them in one PR, majors included. A repo that pins only one of them still gets its PR.
Formatter bumps can reflow existing code and fail the Biome check; label them so they stand out when they do.
Packages carried with a patch-package patch. A bump orphans the version-pinned patch, so group them and never automerge.
